messages.subject: Executive Value Creation Brief | Worley | Global Government Relations
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Burwell,

I am sharing a strategic value creation brief prepared for Worley, focused on government relations, global energy and resources projects, market access, sustainability and institutional risk management. My current work spans government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, strategic partnerships and cross-functional execution in a multinational mining environment.

The attached brief outlines areas where this experience could support government engagement and project delivery across complex markets. I would welcome a short discussion regarding senior leadership or strategic mandates where my background would add value.

Regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Brief for Worley
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Ragunauth Ramsaroop offers a leadership profile aligned with Worley's agenda across government relations, global energy and resources projects, market access, sustainability and institutional risk management. His experience combines government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, strategic partnerships, social performance and executive advisory in a multinational mining environment. He works across operations, legal, finance, procurement, HR, security and technical teams, translating external obligations into coordinated execution. For Worley, his strongest contribution would sit where government engagement, project delivery, customer strategy and sustainability commitments require common governance, early issue visibility and executive accountability across jurisdictions.
strategic_brief.company_context: Worley's 2026 reporting presents a global energy, chemicals and resources business focused on strengthening core markets, expanding into growth markets and scaling technology-enabled project delivery. Its annual reporting also highlights a substantial share of sustainability-related revenue and continued emissions reduction across its own operations. Government relations is therefore closely tied to market access, permitting, industrial policy, energy security, local participation and major-project execution. Clients also expect partners to understand institutional context and stakeholder risk. Leadership with direct experience managing government, ESG and operational interfaces can strengthen country-entry decisions, stakeholder strategy and issue resolution while supporting Worley's wider growth and sustainability ambitions.

opportunities.title: Market access governance
opportunities.rationale: Growth markets require coordinated understanding of government priorities, regulatory requirements, local participation expectations and client investment plans. Structured engagement improves early visibility and supports better strategic decisions.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can build country stakeholder maps, policy issue registers and engagement plans linking government developments to market strategy, project pipelines and accountable business owners.

opportunities.title: Project stakeholder risk
opportunities.rationale: Large energy and resources projects face permitting, community, contractor and institutional issues that can affect schedule, reputation and client confidence if external risks are managed separately from delivery.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can establish cross-functional issue governance connecting government relations with project, legal, sustainability, security and commercial teams around clear actions and escalation thresholds.

opportunities.title: Local value and sustainability alignment
opportunities.rationale: Governments increasingly link project approvals and investment support to local content, workforce, supplier development and sustainability outcomes, requiring credible commitments backed by operating evidence.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can support local-value and sustainability frameworks that connect client commitments, government expectations, procurement, workforce planning and measurable evidence through executive reporting.

days_0_30: Map priority markets, policy issues, project stakeholders and local-value expectations.
days_31_60: Create country engagement, issue and commitment registers with accountable owners.
days_61_90: Launch cross-functional governance for selected market-access and project priorities.
days_91_180: Embed metrics, lessons learned and executive reporting across growth markets.

potential_impact: Stronger government alignment in priority growth markets.
Earlier identification and resolution of project stakeholder risks.
More credible local-value and sustainability commitments.
background_relevance: Government and regulatory relations across multiple public authorities.
ESG, corporate affairs, social performance and strategic partnerships in mining.
Cross-functional coordination with operations, technical, legal, finance, procurement and security teams.
